chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Buck's marriage in Chicago in 1926 and the debts to Nazarro
summary: Bubbles advised against it because Buck owed so much, and says Nazarro kept them in debt through advances.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Oh, yes, that's the biggest mistake he made when he first got married. He got married while we was at the Sunset in Chicago in the year of 1926. When he got married in Chicago thinking he was -- I don't know what he had in mind about where I was concerned to get married because I know his wife thought I didn't want him to get married because I was jealous. I thought that was silly. I said, he doesn't have enough money to get married. Why he'd want to get married, he owes so much money out he hadn't paid yet, and I don't know why he wants to put on more trouble. That's what I told her. But she married him anyway.
He owed so much money to who?

To Nazarro. We both owed money, borrowed money -- what are you talking about? What you talking about? That guy kept us in debt. It's his business. Keeping us in debt, that was his business. He did all right. He did all right.
In other words you'd get an advance on a gig and then you would continually owe him money.
But Buck obviously didn't take your advice.
On getting married, he chose to get married.
That's right. His wife wouldn't take my advice either. I advised her, too. I advised them both. Told her why I'm speaking about him not getting
